questions.question: The demo mints API tokens but has no Supabase project, so `make cashback-demo` cannot sign a *browser* in — its own closing message says so, and F8's browser test needs exactly that. How should a session be established locally and in CI?

options.label: Build the shell token-exchange, flag-gated (Recommended)
options.description: Build the design's second path now — a route that takes a JWKS-verified bearer token and mints a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in production. The demo and Playwright turn it on; the shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a shell. One mechanism serves the demo, the test, and production later.
options.preview:
POST /auth/shell   (enabled only when SHELL_TOKEN_EXCHANGE=1)
  body: token=<jwt from $TMP/reader.token>
  -> verify against JWKS_URL
  -> set our own httpOnly session cookie
  -> 303 to ?next=

production:  flag unset -> 404, button stays disabled
demo / e2e:  flag set   -> Playwright signs in in one POST

options.label: Point the demo at a real Supabase project
options.description: Give scripts/cashback_demo.sh real PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / ANON_KEY for the nonprod project and use the true magic-link flow. Most faithful, but needs credentials in CI and a mailbox the test can read — the nonprod mailer is rate-limited.

options.label: A dev-only sign-in route

# Finishing the cashback member frontend (F1–F9)

## Context

`docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` on `origin/main` is the brief: bring
the member-facing cashback screens in `web/` to the point where one real person
can sign up, opt in, click out to a Linkwise retailer and watch a pending entry
appear in their wallet.

The backend is largely built. What the web cannot do is **sign a member in** —
`pages/[lang]/signin.astro` exists with every control `disabled` and says so on
its own face. Every cashback surface is already wired to an API it can never
present a member token to. Backend gaps B1–B6 (#544–#548) are being worked in
parallel; this plan builds against the documented contract rather than waiting
on them, and says explicitly which proof waits on which gap.

Three founder decisions taken this session:

- **Demo/CI sign-in**: build the design's second path — a route that exchanges a
  bearer token for a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in
  production. The shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a
  shell. The demo and the browser test use the route.
- **Terms**: add a `/{lang}/terms` route so the opt-in cites a readable document.
- **B4**: leave the web's routes on `/api/`; the deploy side narrows the edge
  matcher to `/api/v1/*`. Click-out is proved locally now, on QA when B4 lands.

## Starting state

`xcoder/member-signin` is **fully merged into `origin/main`** (PR #531) and ~30
commits behind it. Every branch below starts fresh from `origin/main`. The
working tree's modified `.claude/`, `.githooks/` and `.entire/` entries are local
tooling and are never committed.

**No issue exists for any of F1–F9.** Each PR below needs one opened first
(`gh issue create`), and dependent chains are bound with `gh stack`.

## What the survey established

**The auth seam already fits a member.** `resolveEditorSession(request, cookies)`
→ `editorSessionFrom(user, token)` → `{ displayName, email, role, token,
authenticated }`, filed in a `WeakMap<Request, …>` and read back synchronously by
`editorSession(request)` (`lib/editorial/session.ts:270–286`). There is **no
`Astro.locals` and no `App.Locals` type**. `roleOf` collapses anything that is
not `editor`/`operator` to `reader` — which is what a member is. `@supabase/ssr`
already exposes `signInWithOtp` and `verifyOtp`; **no new package is needed for
F1.** The middleware never redirects and does not match `/{lang}/signin`.

**`api/tour/[tour].ts` is the pattern** for a route that must keep a bearer token
server-side: it calls `resolveEditorSession` directly rather than trusting the
middleware to have matched its path.

**The design canvas** (26 boards, artifact `059a20a9-…`) draws SignIn almost
exactly as built — shell button primary, email link secondary, no password, no
"check your email" state. It **draws no opt-in screen and no payout-destination
form anywhere**; it asserts the payout requirement in three places
(`SettingsSeam`: *"Money leaves through it, so it cannot live anywhere but with
the module that moves the money"*) and shows both status chips, but never the
screen between them. Those two screens are mine to design. New screens use
`modernist.css`'s own tokens (`--space-N`, `--color-accent-N`, `--ink-muted`,
`--font-heading`), radius 0, hairline borders, no shadows — as `signin.astro`
already does.

**The contract has drifted, and it breaks a real screen.** Verified against the
Go source, not just the OpenAPI document:

| `types.ts` says | Go actually sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` = `…\|'declined'`, no `reserved` | `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` (`earnings/state.go:24–40`, migration 0013 check) — no `declined` |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` — **and the Go comment says "There is no details field and there never will be"** (`payout/handlers.go:430–446`) |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {…}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` (`handlers.go:354–370`) |
| destinations/withdrawals paged | both are `{ items }` with **no `next_cursor`** (`handlers.go:385, 475`) |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required |
| `WalletEntry` | adds `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback`, `hold_rule`; `merchant_name` nullable |

`withdraw.astro` renders `destination.details` and `reserved_amount`, and
`api.destinations()` unwraps a cursor page. **Against the real API the withdrawal
screen does not work today.** This is why the contract PR comes first.

**The member journey's other holes.** `api.optIn()` has zero call sites and
`t.optIn` is rendered nowhere; the wallet's not-participating band links to the
catalogue (`wallet.astro:242–249`). `participation()` is called only by the
wallet, so a non-participant is offered a click. Every member page collapses 401
into `503 + t.emptyQueue` ("nothing open in this list") through one broad catch.
`[slug].astro:82` reads `?clickout=<status>` with `.has()` and discards the code.
Only `rates[0]` is clickable. `next_cursor` is read nowhere. `CashbackNav.astro`
is dead code superseded by `MemberBar.astro`.

## The work

Each numbered item is one issue and one PR, several small commits, every
intermediate commit building and passing. Stacks are bound with `gh stack`.

### 0 — The contract, first *(unblocks everything that touches real data)*

`fix(web): the cashback types say what the api actually sends`

Correct `types.ts` against the Go handlers and `api/openapi.json`; make
`destinations()` and `withdrawals()` read `{ items }`; follow through into
`fixtures.ts`, the `entryStates`/`withdrawalStates` records in
`i18n/cashback.ts`, `withdraw.astro` and `wallet.astro`. This is a *correction*
to a hand-written file, not a contract change — the other two places already
agree. Open a **backend** issue for the one real contract gap: `api/openapi.json`
declares no extension members on `Problem`, while the prose and `withdraw.astro`
both rely on `threshold`/`shortfall` on the 409.

### 1 — F1, member sign-in *(a stack of five)*

1. `feat(web): a session resolves wherever a member signs in` — widen
   `isAuthenticatedPath` to `/{lang}/signin`, `/{lang}/register` and `/auth/*`.
   One mechanical commit renaming `EditorSession` → `Session` (it stops being an
   editor's), leaving `editorSession(request)` as the accessor.
2. `feat(web): the email link signs a member in` — a POST branch calling
   `signInWithOtp({ email, options: { emailRedirectTo } })`, guarded by
   `isSameOrigin` (`lib/csrf.ts:53`); a `/auth/confirm` route calling
   `verifyOtp({ token_hash, type })`, which writes the same `@supabase/ssr`
   httpOnly cookies the editor sign-in writes; a `?next=` return path accepting
   same-origin paths only. New `lib/member/strings.ts` copy for sent / expired /
   refused / not-configured, in `el` and `de`. `signin.test.ts` is **rewritten**:
   it asserts the working page as precisely as it now asserts the disabled one,
   and `member/strings.test.ts`'s "no URL, no `mailto:`, no `http`" rule is
   replaced with rules that fit copy that now describes a mechanism.
3. `feat(web): a signed-in member becomes an account` — after a successful
   callback, `POST /api/v1/account` with the member's own token (B1, #544).
   Until B1 lands that answers 404; the route records it and item 3 of F2 renders
   "your membership is being set up" rather than a 503.
4. `feat(web): the app shell exchanges a token for a session` — `/auth/shell`,
   present only when a new optional `SHELL_TOKEN_EXCHANGE` env field is set.
   **It verifies the token by using it**: one call to `GET /participation` with
   that bearer. A 200 or 404 means the api verified it against `JWKS_URL` *and*
   found an `account` row; a 401 refuses. That needs no JWT library (`jose` is
   not installed and this avoids adding it), cannot drift from the api's own
   verification, and proves membership rather than just signature. On acceptance
   the token goes into our own httpOnly `SameSite=Lax` cookie, read back by a new
   `lib/member/session.ts` resolver that tries this cookie first and falls back to
   `resolveEditorSession`. The shell **button stays disabled with its copy**.
   Record plainly that this session does not refresh — the shell re-hands a token.
5. `feat(web): sign-out, and the chrome that names who is signed in` — a sign-out
   POST mirroring the editor's; `MemberBar`'s `aside` naming the signed-in member;
   the front page's disabled button becoming a link, which retires
   `memberStrings.frontPageButtonState` and its assertion.
6. `feat(web): signing up is the same flow` — `register.astro`'s disabled account
   fields give way to the one email field; the consent panel is untouched.

### 2 — F2, gating

`feat(web): a cashback page without a member sends them to sign in`

One `requireMember(Astro)` used by every `/{lang}/{place}/cashback/…` page: no
session ⇒ redirect to `/{lang}/signin?next=…`; a 401 from the api ⇒ the same;
`/ops` without the operator role ⇒ a 403 page rather than chrome around an empty
queue. The broad catch stops collapsing 401 into `t.emptyQueue`, and gains a
member-facing error string of its own.

### 3 — F3, opt-in *(two PRs)*

1. `feat(web): the cashback terms, on their own route` — `/{lang}/terms`, a
   fourth pane in the legal family, rendering against `brand.legal` and citing
   `legal.documents.terms.version`. Nothing brand-shaped is a literal.
2. `feat(web): a member opts in before they can be paid` — a join screen reached
   when `GET /participation` answers 404, posting
   `brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
   `Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`),
   read from the same `brand.json`. `ErrNoBrand`'s 503 says the deployment names
   no brand and does not retry. The wallet's band points here, not at the
   catalogue.

### 4 — F5, click-out *(three PRs)*

1. `fix(web): the click-out failure says which failure it was` — read the status
   in `?clickout=<status>`; distinct copy for 401, 409, 429 and 502.
2. `feat(web): no click is offered to a member who has not opted in` — the
   merchant page checks participation, and the click-out endpoint refuses,
   until B3 makes the api refuse too.
3. `feat(web): every published band is clickable, not only the first`.

### 5 — F4 and F6, catalogue and wallet

1. `feat(web): the catalogue reads its next page` — `next_cursor` paging, plus
   the design board's ordering disclosure ("the order follows your language and
   your places; no position is sold"). The real endpoint arrives with B2 (#545);
   the fixture keeps development moving meanwhile.
2. `fix(web): the wallet's entry count stops capping at one page`.

### 6 — F7, payout destination

`feat(web): a member adds a payout destination`

`POST /payout-destinations` added to `types.ts`, `api.ts` and the fixtures
(`{ kind, details }` in, a destination with `verified_at: null` out); a screen to
add one; an "awaiting verification" state; `withdraw.astro:301–315`'s dead end
replaced by a link to it. Verification itself is B6 (#548) and is not needed
before the first transaction.

### 7 — F8, the end-to-end test

`test(web): the member journey, in a browser`

Playwright is greenfield — nothing in the repo or CI installs a browser. Tests
live in `web/e2e/`, outside vitest's `src/**/*.test.ts` glob, with their own
config and a new CI job. The test runs against `make cashback-demo` (which starts
Postgres-backed api, the JWKS stand-in minting `$TMP/reader.token`, and `astro
dev` on :4321) and signs in through `/auth/shell` with that token. It walks
sign-in → opt-in → click-out.

### F9 — carried by every PR

Every new string in `el` and `de`, satisfying `i18n/cashback.test.ts`'s four
rules: same key shape and depth, non-empty, **no `€` and no `EUR`**, and every
interpolating function added to the exercised array. Every new page literal-free
from its first commit — `scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` is a per-file ratchet and
a file with no budget entry fails on its first hit. Every new logic module added
to `vitest.config.ts`'s coverage `include`, or it escapes the 80% gate silently.

## Files this touches most

- `web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts`, `api.ts`, `fixtures.ts` — the contract
- `web/src/lib/editorial/session.ts`, `supabase.ts`, `web/src/middleware.ts` — the session
- `web/src/lib/member/strings.ts`, `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts`, `web/src/lib/legal/strings.ts` — copy
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/signin.astro`, `register.astro`, and new `/auth/confirm`, `/auth/shell`, `/{lang}/terms`
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/*.astro` and a new join screen
- `web/astro.config.mjs` — one new optional env field
- `scripts/cashback_demo.sh` — set the exchange flag so the demo's pages stop being fixtures

## Verification

Per PR, before pushing:

```sh
cd web && npm ci && npm run check && npm test && npm run build   # CI `frontend`
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh                                # CI `brand-literals`
make ref-lint                                                    # xcoder/<slug>
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh origin/main..HEAD
```

End to end, locally:

```sh
make cashback-demo          # api + JWKS stand-in + seeded catalogue + web on :4321
# then, in a browser: sign in via /auth/shell with $TMP/reader.token,
# opt in, open a retailer, click out, read the wallet
```

On QA (`https://ra1ze.com`) once B1/B2/B4 land: sign up with a real email link,
opt in, click out, and record in the PR what was run and what was seen — then
update `docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` in the same PR.

## What genuinely waits on the backend

- **Sign-up producing a member** waits on B1 (#544). Everything before it builds
  and is proved locally with the demo's minted tokens.
- **The catalogue on the real endpoint** waits on B2 (#545); the page and the
  fixture already work.
- **Click-out proved in a browser on QA** waits on B4 (#546). Proved locally now.
- **The legal pages on QA** wait on B5 (#547).
- **A withdrawal** waits on B6 (#548), and is not part of the first transaction.

cd C:/Users/madym/repos/apivo-news && gh issue create --title "The web's cashback types disagree with what the api sends, and the withdrawal screen cannot work" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts` is hand-written against the contract and checked
by nothing. It has drifted from the Go handlers far enough that one screen is
broken against a real API rather than merely imprecise.

Verified against the Go source, not only `api/openapi.json`:

| `types.ts` says | the api sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` includes `declined`, omits `reserved` | `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` — `internal/cashback/earnings/state.go:24-40`, and migration 0013's `entry_state_known` check. There is no `declined`. |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` — `internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go:437-446`, whose comment reads "There is no details field and there never will be". |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {...}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` — `handlers.go:354-370`. |
| both lists are cursor pages | both answer `{ items }` with no `next_cursor` — `handlers.go:385` and `:475`. |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable. |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required. |
| `WalletEntry` | adds `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback` and `hold_rule`, and `merchant_name` is nullable. |

The consequence is not theoretical. `withdraw.astro` renders
`destination.details` and `reserved_amount` on every row of a member's
withdrawal history, and `api.destinations()` unwraps a cursor page that the
endpoint does not return. Against the deployed api that screen renders blanks.

This is a correction to the one place that was never checked. `http-api.md` and
`api/openapi.json` already agree with the Go; only the TypeScript does not.

Fix `types.ts`, then follow it through `api.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, the
`entryStates`/`withdrawalStates` records in `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts`, and the
two pages that read the changed fields.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

cd C:/Users/madym/repos/apivo-news && cat > /tmp/issue_ops.json <<'JSONEOF'
{
  "title": "GET /ops/withdrawals is called by the operator queue and is not implemented",
  "body": "`web/src/lib/cashback/api.ts:389` calls `GET /api/v1/cashback/ops/withdrawals?state=awaiting_approval`, and `web/src/pages/ops/withdrawals.astro` renders the queue from it.

The route does not exist. `internal/cashback/ops/handler.go:83-98` registers only the three decisions:

```
"POST " + Prefix + "withdrawals/{id}/approve": h.approveWithdrawal,
"POST " + Prefix + "withdrawals/{id}/reject":  h.rejectWithdrawal,
"POST " + Prefix + "withdrawals/{id}/settle":  h.settleWithdrawal,
```

`api/openapi.json` carries the same three and no listing.

This is the same shape of gap as #545: documented in the contract's operator section, called by the web, absent from the api. C-4 says a named human approves every payout — and the screen that names them cannot list what is waiting.

The member-side counterpart `GET /withdrawals` exists (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go:385`) and answers `{ items }` with rows of `request_id`, `destination_id`, `amount`, `state`, `requested_at`, `decided_at`, `decision_reason`, `payout_reference`. An operator queue needs the account behind each row as well, which the member view deliberately omits.

Until it lands the operator withdrawal queue is a fixture-only screen."
}
JSONEOF
gh api repos/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/issues --input /tmp/issue_ops.json --jq '"CREATED #\(.number) \(.html_url)"' 2>&1 | tail -2
cat > /tmp/issue_problem.json <<'JSONEOF'
{
  "title": "api/openapi.json declares no extension members on Problem, so the withdrawal 409 is undocumented",
  "body": "`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/contracts/http-api.md` says a withdrawal refused below the threshold answers 409 with `threshold` and `shortfall` as RFC 9457 extension members, and `web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro:117-139` builds the member's refusal sentence out of exactly those two figures.

`api/openapi.json`'s `Problem` schema declares `type`, `title`, `status` and `detail` and nothing else. A client generated from the document would not know the figures exist, and the CI validation cannot notice if they stop being sent.

Add the extension members the contract promises — `code`, `threshold`, `shortfall`, `confirmed`, `requested` — to the `Problem` schema, so the three places that describe this API agree."
}
JSONEOF

is written in, whether that language is a fallback, and the rule holding a
held entry back. WalletEntry declared none of the four, so the page could not

    there was no click, so there is no route back to a shop (FR-034). The

  * a name that answered in the retailer's own language is labelled, as the
    catalogue already labels it (US5 scenario 2), instead of being passed
    off as the member's own language.
  * a held entry names the rule holding it. "In review" alone does not tell
    a member whether the review is about them.

The preview gains a held entry and a hand-attributed one, because a fixture
set that never produces the null is a fixture set that lets a blank line

nothing to do with the place axis a member browses under. Terms is the

fix(web): a payout destination is a rail and a date, not a masked account (#554)

PayoutDestination declared `id` and a `details` string described as a masked
IBAN. The api has never sent either. It sends destination_id, kind,
verified_at, verified_method and created_at, and the handler says why in as
many words: "There is no details field and there never will be" - the account
lives where this service cannot read it (ADR-0003), and an endpoint echoing it
would be the leak the arrangement exists to prevent.

So the withdrawal screen was printing `undefined` in a monospace span on every
destination it offered and on every past request, against any real
deployment. It now names a destination by what the api actually sends: the
rail, and the day it was added. That is enough to tell apart the one or two
destinations anybody has, and it is all there is.

Withdrawal loses `reserved_amount` and the nested destination for the same
reason. The reserved figure belongs to the 201 that commits a member to it -
where the whole-entries rule can surprise them - and not to a historical row,
where the amount is the amount. The destination arrives as an id, which the
page resolves against the member's own list, and says so plainly when a
withdrawal cites one that is no longer there.

WithdrawalForApproval is left as it stands, with a note: no endpoint serves
it. The operator queue calls GET /ops/withdrawals and the api registers only
the three decisions on that prefix.
MSGEOF

import json, io
body = """Closes #554.

`web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts` is hand-written against the contract and checked by nothing. It had drifted from the Go handlers far enough that a screen was broken against a real API rather than merely imprecise, and the drift was invisible because every page renders from fixtures that agreed with the wrong types.

Each commit corrects one group of fields together with everything that reads them, so every intermediate commit builds and passes.

### What was wrong

| `types.ts` said | the api sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` includes `declined`, omits `reserved` | the six in `internal/cashback/earnings/state.go:24-40` and in migration 0013's `entry_state_known` check. There is no `declined`. |
| `WalletEntry` has a non-null `merchant_name` and no language | `merchant_name` is null for a hand-attributed entry (FR-034), and it carries `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback` and `hold_rule` |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required (FR-003) |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable — a band with no published end |
| `MerchantDetail` has no `country`, no `terms` | `internal/cashback/catalogue/handlers.go:170-199` sends both |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {...}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` |
| both of those are cursor pages | both answer `{ items }` and no cursor |

### The one that was not cosmetic

`web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro` named every destination by `destination.details`, described in the type as a masked IBAN. The api has never sent that field, and `internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go:430-436` says why in as many words:

> There is no details field and there never will be. What a member sees is which rail it is for and whether it has been proved theirs; the details are somewhere this service cannot read them from (ADR-0003), and an endpoint that echoed them would be the leak the whole arrangement exists to prevent.

So against any real deployment that screen printed `undefined` on every destination it offered and on every past request, and the same on the operator queue.

A destination is now named by what the api actually sends: the rail, and the day it was added. That is enough to tell apart the one or two anybody has, and it is all there is. `Withdrawal` loses `reserved_amount` for a related reason — the reserved figure belongs to the `201` that commits a member to it, where the whole-entries rule can surprise them, and not to a historical row where the amount is the amount.

### Fixtures

The preview gains a held entry naming its hold rule, and one attributed by hand with no retailer at all. A fixture set that never produces the null is a fixture set that lets a blank line reach a member unnoticed.

### Two backend gaps found on the way, filed rather than patched here

- #556 — `GET /ops/withdrawals` is called by the operator queue and is not implemented. Same shape as #545. `WithdrawalForApproval` is left as it stands with a note saying so.
- #557 — `api/openapi.json` declares no extension members on `Problem`, while the contract prose and the withdrawal screen both rely on `threshold` and `shortfall` on the 409.

### Checked

- `npm run check` — 0 errors
- `npm test` — 902 passing. `src/lib/astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under full-suite load on this Windows machine; an unmodified `origin/main` worktree fails the same two cases with the same timings, so it is not this branch. Recorded on #132, which already tracks that class.
- `npm run build` — clean
- brand-literal lint — no name, host or colour literal in any changed file, and none of them carries a budget entry
- `lint-refs.sh` on the branch and over the range, `lint-commit-authors.sh` over the range"""
io.open('/tmp/pr554.json','w',encoding='utf-8').write(json.dumps({
  "title": "The cashback types say what the api actually sends",
  "head": "xcoder/cashback-contract-truth",
  "base": "main",
  "body": body,
}))
print("ok")
PYEOF

feat(web): a return path that cannot leave this site (#564)

Sign-in is reached from somewhere and has to send the member back. That is a
`next` parameter, and a `next` parameter is the one place where being
approximately right is an open redirect.

The check is on the SHAPE of the string rather than on a parsed URL, because
`new URL(raw, origin)` resolves `//evil.example` against this origin, reports
it as valid, and hands back another site. It begins with a slash, so every
test anybody writes in a hurry passes it.

Refused, with a case each: an absolute URL; a relative path, whose meaning
depends on where it is read; `//host` and `/\host`, both protocol-relative
once a browser has normalised the backslash; anything carrying a control
character, which is how a URL gets split; and this flow's own `/auth/...`
routes, where landing after finishing a sign-in is a loop rather than a
return.

A refusal is never an error. Somebody arriving with a mangled parameter still
wants to sign in, so they sign in and land on the fallback.

Also here because they are the same subject: the outcomes a redirect can hand
the sign-in page, and the absolute URL an auth provider is configured to send
somebody back to. It carries the language, because that route has none of its
own and a failure needs explaining in the language being read.

The module joins vitest.config.ts's coverage list in the same commit. A logic
file left off that list escapes the gate silently, which is worse than not
having one.

content.text:
Three PRs are open and fully green. Here's where things stand.

## What I found first

The master prompt isn't in your checkout — this branch is ~30 commits behind and `xcoder/member-signin` is already merged (PR #531). I read the brief from `origin/main` and started every branch fresh from there.

Then a survey turned up something the brief didn't predict: **`types.ts` had drifted far enough from the Go handlers to break a screen**. `PayoutDestination.details` — which `withdraw.astro` prints on every destination and every past withdrawal — has never been sent by the api. The handler says so in as many words: *"There is no details field and there never will be."* Against any real deployment that screen renders `undefined`. `EntryState` also carried a `declined` nothing produces and was missing `reserved`, which does arrive.

That reordered the work: the contract had to come first.

## Shipped

| PR | What | CI |
|---|---|---|
| [#561](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/561) | The cashback types say what the api actually sends (closes #554) | green |
| [#563](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/563) | The session belongs to whoever is signed in, and resolves where they sign in (closes #562) | green |
| [#565](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/565) | **Member sign-in: the email path** (closes #564), stacked on #563 | green |

**#565 is F1's core.** `signInWithOtp` sends a link; `/auth/confirm` exchanges it for the same `@supabase/ssr` session the editor sign-in produces. A first link creates the account, so sign-up and sign-in are one act. No password anywhere — which is also why there's no reset screen to build. The confirm route accepts both a `token_hash` and a PKCE `code`, because which one arrives depends on the project's email template and I couldn't verify that without the Supabase keys.

The shell button stays disabled with its copy, as the design requires. The front page's button became a link, and `register.astro` stopped claiming registration was pending — it had a disabled *password* field, which this product has decided never to have.

Tests were rewritten, not relaxed. `signin.test.ts` asserted "no form, no method, no action"; it now asserts the new promise just as tightly, including that no state renders a password field.

## Also filed

- **#556** — `GET /ops/withdrawals` is called by the operator queue and isn't implemented. Same shape as #545; the queue is fixture-only until it lands.
- **#557** — `openapi.json` declares no `Problem` extensions, while the contract and the withdrawal screen both rely on `threshold`/`shortfall`.
- **#132** — added evidence that `astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under full-suite load. I verified this on an unmodified `origin/main` worktree before attributing it to load rather than my changes; with `--testTimeout=30000` all 963 tests pass.

## Not proved

The link has never been sent by a real provider from this branch — that needs the nonprod keys on a deployment. It's the first thing to check on QA once #565 and #544 land.

## Next, if you want me to continue

F1.4 (the flag-gated shell exchange, which is what unblocks the browser test), F2 gating, F3 opt-in plus the `/{lang}/terms` route, then F7's payout-destination screen. Worth knowing: the design canvas draws **neither** an opt-in screen nor a payout-destination form — I checked all 26 boards. Those two are mine to design, and I've noted it so it isn't rediscovered later.

content.text:
All three are `clean`, and I verified the fully-merged result builds and passes before answering.

## Merge order

```
1.  #561  The cashback types say what the api actually sends       base: main
2.  #563  The session belongs to whoever is signed in              base: main
3.  #565  Member sign-in: the email path                           base: #563's branch
```

**#561 and #563 are independent** — either can go first. **#565 must come after #563**; it's stacked on it, and GitHub will retarget it to `main` automatically when #563 merges.

I put #561 first because it fixes a screen that is broken today: `withdraw.astro` renders `destination.details`, a field the api has never sent, so against QA it prints `undefined` on every destination and every past withdrawal.

**Verified, not assumed:** I built a scratch worktree at `main + #561 + #563 + #565` and ran it — 0 typecheck errors, 969 tests passing, clean build, `no unaccounted brand literals`. Four files are touched by both #561 and #563 (`wallet.astro`, `withdraw.astro`, `ops/withdrawals.astro`, `OpsLayout.astro`); they merge cleanly in either order.

## The backend gaps — confirmed closed, and they matter

| | State | What it changes for the frontend |
|---|---|---|
| **B1** #544 | closed | `POST /api/v1/account` → `{id, email, display_name, role}`. F1.3 is now buildable for real. Two refusals to handle: a token with no email claim, and an email already held by another account. |
| **B2** #545 | closed | `GET /catalogue` landed with **exactly** the shape `api.catalogue()` already calls — `lang` required, repeatable `place`, `q`/`limit`/`cursor`, `{items, next_cursor}`. F4 collapses from "wire it" to "verify it and read `next_cursor`". |
| **B4** #546 | closed | Landed as `only /api/v1/* goes to the api` — the option we picked. The web's own `/api/cashback/clickout` now reaches the web on Hetzner, so F5 is provable on QA. |
| **B5** #547 | closed | The web gets `BRAND_DIR`, so F3's opt-in can read the terms version on QA. |
| **B6** #548 | **open** | Payout-destination verification. Expected — the brief says it isn't needed before the first transaction. |

Still open from what I filed: **#556** (`GET /ops/withdrawals` is called by the operator queue and isn't implemented — same shape as #545) and **#557** (`Problem` extensions missing from `openapi.json`).

Main has moved 23 commits but touched **nothing under `web/`**, so no rebase is needed on any of the three.

## After you merge

The path shortens because of what the backend landed. Next up, in order: **F1.3** account provisioning on the sign-in callback (now unblocked by B1), **F1.4** the flag-gated shell token exchange (which is what lets the browser test sign in), **F2** gating, then **F3** opt-in plus the `/{lang}/terms` route.

#564 wired the email link: a member signs in and gets a session carrying a verified token. The api does not know them. `account` has no row for that subject, so every cashback route answers 401 (`ErrUnknownAccount`) and the wallet, the catalogue and the click-out all fail for somebody who has just successfully signed in — the worst state to be in, because everything looks right.

#544 landed the endpoint that fixes it. `POST /api/v1/account` takes no body, reads the subject and the email out of the verified token, and either creates the row as a `reader` or answers the one already there. It never changes a role, so calling it on every sign-in is safe and a second call is harmless.

**`/auth/confirm` calls it, once, straight after the exchange.** That is the only moment the web holds a fresh token and knows the sign-in just succeeded.

Its refusals are not all the same, and the difference is the work here:

- **200 / 201** — the account exists. Onward.
- **409** — the token's email already belongs to a different account. A real refusal a person must be told about, not a transient one: they have signed in and they cannot be a member under that address. The session is dropped rather than left standing, because a session that can reach nothing is worse than none.
- **400** — the token carries no email. A provider misconfiguration rather than the member's fault.
- **401 / 500 / unreachable** — transient, or a deployment with no api configured at all. Sign-in still succeeded; the member goes on to where they were headed, and the gating work will explain what they find there.

The client belongs in its own module with its own tests, as the cashback one does — the outcome mapping is the whole substance and it should not live inside a route."""}))

import { CashbackApiError, type CashbackSource } from '../cashback/api';
import type { Session } from '../editorial/session';

/**
 * Who may see a cashback surface, and what happens to everybody else
 * (issue #570).
 *
 * There is no anonymous cashback surface — every route answers 401 without a
 * token, the catalogue included (FR-023). So the question each of the four
 * member pages has to answer is the same one, and it has three answers that
 * a page writing its own version will get subtly wrong:
 *
 *   * nobody is signed in — send them to sign in, and bring them back
 *   * the api refused the token they have — the same, because to a member
 *     those are one situation, and since #567 the usual cause is an account
 *     row that has not been created yet
 *   * anything else — a 503, which is the deployment's problem and not theirs
 *
 * FIXTURE MODE IS EXEMPT, and that exemption is the reason this is a module
 * rather than a one-line check. A pull-request preview has no api and nobody
 * signed in, and its entire job is to render the screens for review;
 * redirecting there would make previews useless for the one thing they are
 * for. The rule is not "is there a session" but "is there an api that would
 * refuse us".
 */

/**
 * Whether this page must send the visitor to sign in before rendering.
 *
 * `source` is the client's own answer to "am I talking to a real api", which
 * is the only honest way to ask: a page cannot tell a missing `API_BASE_URL`
 * from a preview stamp by looking at the session.
 */
export function needsSignIn(session: Session, source: CashbackSource): boolean {
  return source !== 'fixture' && !session.authenticated;
}

/**
 * Whether a failure from the cashback client was the api declining to
 * recognise the caller.
 *
 * 401 and 403 both mean it: 401 is no token or one that does not verify, 403
 * is a token that verifies for somebody this route is not for. Neither is a
 * state a member can wait out, and both are cured by signing in — which,
 * after #567, also creates the account row when it is missing.
 */
export function isUnauthorized(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof CashbackApiError && (error.status === 401 || error.status === 403);
}

import io, re

PAGES = [
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/index.astro',
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/[slug].astro',
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/wallet.astro',
  'web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro',
]

GATE = """    // FR-023: there is no anonymous cashback surface. Sending somebody to
    // sign in is the answer to that, and a 503 saying nothing is not.
    if (needsSignIn(session, api.source)) {
      return Astro.redirect(signInPath(lang, { next: here }));
    }
"""

CATCH = """} catch (error) {
  // A token the api will not accept is, to a member, the same situation as
  // no token at all - and since #567 the usual cause is an account row that
  // has not been created yet, which signing in again creates.
  if (isUnauthorized(error)) {
    return Astro.redirect(signInPath(lang, { next: here }));
  }
"""

for p in PAGES:
    s = io.open(p,'rb').read().decode('utf-8'); crlf='\r\n' in s
    b = s.replace('\r\n','\n')

    # 1. The path to come back to, declared beside the session it guards.
    m = re.search(r"^const session = sessionOf\(Astro\.request\);$", b, re.M)
    assert m, p + ": no session line"
    b = b[:m.end()] + "\n// Where signing in should bring them back to, query and all: a member\n// sent away from a filtered wallet wants that wallet back, not the top of it.\nconst here = `${Astro.url.pathname}${Astro.url.search}`;" + b[m.end():]

    # 2. The gate, immediately after the client is built.
    m = re.search(r"^(  api = createCashbackApi\(API_BASE_URL, \{\n(?:.*\n)*?  \}\);\n)", b, re.M)
    assert m, p + ": no createCashbackApi call"
    b = b[:m.end(1)] + GATE + b[m.end(1):]

    # 3. The 401 branch, first thing in the catch.
    old_catch = "} catch (error) {\n"
    i = b.index(old_catch, m.end(1))
    b = b[:i] + CATCH + b[i+len(old_catch):]

    # 4. Imports.
    anchor = "import { frontPagePath, parseAxes }"
    assert b.count(anchor) == 1, p + ": import anchor"
    b = b.replace(anchor,
        "import { signInPath } from '../../../../lib/member/access';\n"
        "import { isUnauthorized, needsSignIn } from '../../../../lib/member/gate';\n" + anchor)

    io.open(p,'wb').write((b.replace('\n','\r\n') if crlf else b).encode('utf-8'))
    print('gated', p.split('/')[-1])

import { CashbackApiError } from '../cashback/api';
import { isReadingLanguage, type ReadingLanguage } from '../reader/axes';

/**
 * Who may see a cashback surface, and what happens to everybody else
 * (issue #570).
 *
 * There is no anonymous cashback surface — every route answers 401 without a
 * token, the catalogue included (FR-023). That is a property of the whole
 * product, not of any one page, so the fence stands in the middleware beside
 * the crawler fence rather than being remembered separately by each of the
 * four member pages. A fifth page added later is gated by existing.
 *
 * FIXTURE MODE IS EXEMT FROM IT, and that exemption is the reason this is a
 * decision rather than a one-line check. A pull-request preview runs with no
 * api and nobody signed in, and its entire job is to render the screens for
 * review; redirecting there would make previews useless for the one thing
 * they exist for. So the question is not "is somebody signed in" but "is
 * there an api here that would refuse them".
 */

/** Whether this visitor must sign in before a cashback page will render. */
export function needsSignIn(authenticated: boolean, fixtures: boolean): boolean {
  return !fixtures && !authenticated;
}

/**
 * The reading language of a member cashback page, or null for anything else.
 *
 * Only `/{lang}/{place}/cashback…` is matched. `/ops` has a role of its own to
 * check and no language in its path, and `/api/cashback/…` is posted to by a
 * form — answering a POST with a redirect to a sign-in page would lose what
 * was posted, so that route keeps its own refusal.
 *
 * A language this application does not serve answers null rather than a
 * default: the page's own guard rewrites those to /404, and a fence that
 * redirected them to a Greek sign-in would be inventing a reader's language
 * on the way past (FR-009, FR-015).
 */
export function cashbackPageLanguage(pathname: string): ReadingLanguage | null {
  const match = /^\/([^/]+)\/[^/]+\/cashback(?:\/|$)/.exec(pathname);
  const lang = match?.[1];
  return lang !== undefined && isReadingLanguage(lang) ? lang : null;
}

/**
 * Whether a failure from the cashback client was the api declining to
 * recognise the caller.
 *
 * 401 and 403 both mean it: 401 is no token or one that does not verify, 403
 * is a token that verifies for somebody this route is not for.
 *
 * Note what pages must NOT do with this: redirect. Past the middleware fence
 * there IS a session, so a 401 here means the api does not recognise a person
 * who is signed in — an account row that was never created (#567), or a token
 * this deployment's JWKS will not verify. Sending them to sign in would
 * return them to the same 401 and the same redirect, forever. The page says
 * so instead, and offers the sign-in as a choice rather than taking it.
 */
export function isUnauthorized(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof CashbackApiError && (error.status === 401 || error.status === 403);
}

body = """Closes #570. Independent of #569 — they touch different files and either can merge first.

**FR-023: there is no anonymous cashback surface.** Every api route answers 401 without a token, the catalogue included. Until now each of the four member pages caught that 401 in the same broad `catch` that catches a dead container, so a signed-out visitor was shown:

> *nothing open in this list*

— `t.emptyQueue`, an operator's sentence about a work queue — under a **503** saying the deployment is broken. Three unrelated situations, one indistinguishable answer.

### The fence goes in the middleware

Beside the crawler fence, for the reason that one is there: this is a property of the product, not of a page, and four pages each remembering it is four chances to forget. **A fifth page is fenced by existing.**

It fences the member pages only. `/ops` has a role of its own to check and no language in its path; `/api/cashback/…` is posted to by a form, where answering with a redirect to a sign-in page would lose what was posted.

Two things it deliberately does not do:

- **Fixture mode is exempt.** A pull-request preview runs with no api and nobody signed in, and its whole job is to render the screens for review. Fencing it would make previews useless for the one thing they exist for.
- **A language this application does not serve is left alone.** The page's own guard rewrites those to `/404`; a fence that redirected them to a Greek sign-in would be inventing a reader's language on the way past (FR-009, FR-015).

The return path carries the query, because somebody sent away from a filtered wallet wants that wallet back and not the top of it.

### The 401 that survives the fence must not redirect

Past the fence there **is** a session, so a 401 from the api means it does not recognise somebody who is signed in — an account row that was never created (#567), or a token this deployment's JWKS will not verify.

Redirecting that to sign-in comes straight back, gets the same 401, and redirects again. **That is an infinite loop**, and it is the reason the pages say what happened and offer signing in again as a *choice* rather than taking it — which is also the cure, since the callback registers the account on the way through. They answer `403` while they do: the request was understood and refused, not broken.

### One decision, asked from two places

The fence needs to know whether this deployment answers from fixtures, and it is not building a client. `answersFromFixtures` is lifted out of `createCashbackApi` rather than restated, and a table-driven case pins the two together over every combination that matters. A restated copy would drift, and the way that drift would surface is a preview redirecting reviewers away from the screens they came to see.

### Copy

Every failure a member can now reach has a sentence written for a member, in `el` and `de`. The wallet's signed-out band stays, with a comment saying why: signed out is the middleware's answer now, so that band is reachable only in fixture mode — exactly the state a reviewer on a preview is in.

### A note for whoever touches frontmatter next

The first shape I wrote put the gate in each page as `if (needsSignIn(…)) return Astro.redirect(signInPath(lang, { next: here }));`. `astro check` reports `here` and the `signInPath` import as **unused**. It is not the `try`, not `Astro.redirect`, and not the condition — I tested all three. **`astro check` does not count a local whose only read is inside a frontmatter block that `return`s**, whatever the redirect mechanism. Worth knowing before somebody spends an hour on it; it also pushed this to the middleware, which is where it belonged.

### Checked

- `npm run check` — 0 errors
- `npm test` — 1018 passing (55 new), coverage 95% statements / 94.4% branches / 90.4% functions
- `npm run build` — clean
- brand-literal lint — clean on a worktree with no untracked files
- `lint-refs.sh` on the branch and over the range, `lint-commit-authors.sh` over the range"""

Both green. Here's the state.

## Merged, and confirmed on `main`

#561, #563, #565 all landed. `main` moved 23 commits from the backend side but touched nothing under `web/`, so nothing needed rebasing.

## Two new PRs, both fully green

| PR | What | Closes |
|---|---|---|
| [#569](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/569) | **Signing in makes the member an account** | #567 |
| [#573](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/573) | **A cashback page without a member sends them to sign in** | #570 |

They're independent — either order, no conflicts.

**#569** closes the gap #565 left open. A session isn't an account: every cashback route looks the caller up in `account` and 401s when there's no row, so a member who signed in successfully found the wallet, catalogue and click-out all failing while nothing *looked* broken. `/auth/confirm` now calls `POST /api/v1/account` (your #544) straight after the exchange. The interesting part is the refusals: a 409 (address already another account's) drops the session and says what to try instead, because a session that reaches nothing is worse than none; an unreachable api lands with the *successes*, because a preview has none at all.

**#573** puts the sign-in fence in the middleware rather than in four pages — same reasoning as the crawler fence already there, and a fifth page gets fenced by existing. Previews stay exempt, or they'd redirect reviewers away from the screens they exist to show.

One thing worth flagging from #573: the obvious shape — `if (needsSignIn(…)) return Astro.redirect(signInPath(…))` in each page — makes `astro check` report the locals as **unused**. I tested it three ways: it's not the `try`, not `Astro.redirect`, not the condition. `astro check` doesn't count a local whose only read sits inside a frontmatter block that `return`s. It's in the PR body so the next person doesn't lose an hour to it. It also pushed the fence to the middleware, which is where it belonged.

I also found and avoided a real trap: redirecting on a 401 *past* the fence is an infinite loop, since the member does have a session. Those pages state the situation and offer sign-in as a choice.

## What's next

F3, with your answer: I'll write `/{lang}/terms` as a plain-language statement of what the code actually enforces — rate snapshotted at click, pending until the shop confirms, reversed on a refund, paid only to a destination proved yours above the threshold, leaving keeps the records. Each line traceable to a mechanism, no invented obligations. Then the opt-in screen posting `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`, which is the exact field `Participations.Join` compares.

After that: F1.4 (the flag-gated shell exchange, which unblocks the browser test), then F4/F5/F6 verification against the now-live catalogue endpoint.

One housekeeping note: `main` now tracks `.mcp.json` with the IcePanel server, which displaced my local one configuring graft. I backed the local copy up rather than lose it. If you want both, that's a one-line addition to the tracked file — say the word and I'll fold it into a chore commit.

In terms of F3 I'll follow your lead, for F1.4 and F4/F5/F6 let's plan and act accordingly. Prioritise the housekeeping detail, i want them both to be available please. create a small pr for that. In fact on housekeeping, do you mind also cleaning up the stale gh issues? I reckon there are many that have been alread implemented but where never referenced therefore never closed.

# Housekeeping, then F3 · F1.4 · F4–F6

## Context

Five PRs have merged (#561, #563, #565, #569 pending, #573 pending) and the
backend closed B1, B2, B4 and B5. Two of the founder's own housekeeping items
now come first, then the remaining frontend work on the path to one real
transaction.

The founder asked for, in priority order:

1. **`.mcp.json` carries both servers.** `main` now tracks it with IcePanel
   only, which displaced a local file configuring graft. Both are wanted.
2. **Close the stale issues.** Many were implemented but never referenced by a
   PR, so nothing auto-closed them.
3. **F3** — opt-in and the terms route, on my own judgement (settled: I draft
   the terms as a statement of what the code enforces, each line traceable).
4. **F1.4 and F4/F5/F6** — planned and executed.

*(F1.4 and F4–F6 sections pending exploration results.)*

---

## 1 — `.mcp.json`: both servers *(one small PR, first)*

`main` tracks:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "icepanel": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.icepanel.io/mcp" } } }
```

The displaced local file configured graft as a stdio server
(`npx -y @nanonets/graft mcp`). Both belong in the tracked file — graft is
already a first-class part of how this repo is navigated (there is a
`.claude/skills/graft/` and a SessionStart hook that points at it).

**One thing that goes stale with it**, and it is the reason this is a PR and
not a one-line edit: `docs/architecture/icepanel-model.md:2030` says the file
*"names a server and nothing else"*, and
`docs/architecture/README.md:85` points at it. The sentence stops being true
the moment a second server is added, so it changes in the same commit.

Nothing validates `.mcp.json` — no script, workflow or Makefile target reads
it — so there is no check to extend.

---

## 2 — Stale issues: close what the tree proves is built

The founder's read is right, and the evidence is entirely local — which
matters, because **GitHub's secondary rate limit is currently refusing this
account's content requests**, and any plan that needs one API call per issue
will stall. The method below needs two or three reads and one write per issue
actually closed.

### The evidence, gathered without the API

Three independent signals, all computable from the tree:

| Signal | How | Found |
|---|---|---|
| A commit on `main` names the issue | `git log --format=%s` → `(#N)` | **173 distinct numbers** |
| Code or config cites the issue | `git grep '#NNN'` over `internal/ web/src/ cmd/ scripts/ deploy/` | **83 numbers** |
| The artifact the issue names exists | issue title names a file/symbol; check the tree | per issue |

Union of the first two: **197 issue numbers with implementation evidence.**
Intersecting that with the open-issue list is the candidate set.

### Why the obvious source is not usable

`specs/*/tasks.md` checkboxes look authoritative and are not.
`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/tasks.md` reports 81 done / 66 open, yet
T001–T006 are all unchecked and all plainly built — the cashback config keys,
the `blnk`/`redis` compose services, the `cashback` CI job. The checkboxes
have the same drift the issues do. **Evidence comes from code and history,
never from a checkbox.**

### How each issue is judged

- **Tier A — close.** A commit subject on `main` carries `(#N)`. That is the
  repository's own convention for "this commit did that", and an issue still
  open under one was simply never referenced by a PR body. Closed with a
  comment citing the commits.
- **Tier B — verify, then close or leave.** No commit reference, but the title
  names a concrete artifact (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go`, a route,
  a symbol). Check the artifact and its tests. `#242` is the shape of this:
  no commit cites it, and every handler it asks for exists.
- **Tier C — leave open, and list.** Anything ambiguous, anything for an
  unbuilt feature (the `003-cashback-claims` backlog, #448–#492, is not
  built), and anything where the artifact exists but the issue asks for more
  than the artifact.

Tier C is reported to the founder rather than guessed at. A wrongly closed
issue is a task that quietly stops existing.

### Rate-limit discipline

Two or three reads to list the open issues, then all judgement is local. Each
close is one `PATCH` (`state: closed`, `state_reason: completed`) plus one
comment. Batched with pauses and resumable from a written work-list, so a
secondary limit part-way through costs nothing but time.

*(remaining sections pending)*

---

## 3 — F3: the terms, and the opt-in *(two PRs)*

### 3a — `/{lang}/terms`

Its own route in the legal family — same layout, masthead and language
switcher as `/{lang}/impressum` — but **not** a fourth `LegalPane`.
`LegalPane` renders term/value pairs out of `brand.legal` (entity, address,
jurisdiction); the cashback terms are prose, and forcing them through it would
distort a component that currently does one thing well.

Content lives in a new `web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts` beside
`lib/legal/strings.ts`, in `el` and `de`, with the version rendered from
`brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
`Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`).

Each clause states a rule the code actually enforces, and nothing else:

| Clause | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| the rate shown when you clicked is the rate that applies | FR-013, the band snapshotted onto the click |
| an entry is pending until the shop confirms it | `earnings/state.go` — `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` |
| a refund reverses it, and both rows stay visible | `reversal_of_id`, US3 scenario 2 |
| money is paid only to an account proved yours | FR-051, `verified_at` |
| there is a floor before a payout | `payout_threshold` |
| leaving stops the earning and keeps the records | FR-003 — a status and a date, never a deletion |
| balances are a claim on a future rebate | founder decision Q2, ADR-0002 |

No invented obligations, no boilerplate, and the PR says plainly that
counsel-approved text replaces this before launch.

**Not** linked from the site footer. That carries the three notices a
German-facing service legally owes; these are product terms, reached from the
opt-in screen and from the wallet.

### 3b — the opt-in screen

Reached when `GET /participation` answers 404 — which is not an error, and the
contract says so. Posts `brand.legal.documents.terms.version`; a 400 means the
version moved under the member and the page reloads rather than re-posting a
stale consent; a 503 means the deployment names no brand (`ErrNoBrand`) and
the page says so rather than retrying.

The wallet's not-participating band stops pointing at the catalogue and points
here. `api.optIn()` has existed with zero call sites since it was written.

*(F1.4 and F4–F6 pending exploration results)*

## 7 — F1.4: the app-shell token exchange *(two PRs)*

This is what lets a browser be signed in with no Supabase project, which is
what F8's Playwright test needs. The survey turned up three facts that shape
it, and one that is a bug in the demo.

**`/auth/shell` needs no middleware change.** `isAccessPath` already matches
`/^\/auth(?:\/|$)/` (`middleware.ts:182-186`), so the route is already an
authenticated path, already gets `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and a
shell session automatically satisfies `fenceCashback` because that reads
`sessionOf()` like everything else.

**There is no crypto in `web/`** — no `jose`, no `node:crypto`, no HMAC, no
signed cookie. That settles the design rather than blocking it: the cookie
holds the bearer token verbatim and **the api stays the only verifier**, which
is exactly what `resolveSession` already does (it never trusts cookie contents
either — it round-trips to the auth server). The exchange confirms the token
once by calling the api with it, and the session resolver confirms it again on
each request, parallel to Supabase's `getUser()` and at the same cost.

non-Supabase cookie with a narrow `PreferenceCookieStore` interface that keeps
the module testable without Astro. It also records why `__Host-` was rejected —
it mandates `Secure` and the demo runs on plain http. Same trade here;
`isSecureRequest` decides `Secure`.

   one fact, and lets the exchange reuse `registerAccount` unchanged rather
   than growing a second code path for the demo's benefit.

transaction.

1. **`.mcp.json` carries both servers.** `main` now tracks it with IcePanel

2. **Close the stale issues.** Many were implemented but never referenced by a

3. **F3** — opt-in and the terms route, on my own judgement (settled: I draft

4. **F1.4 and F4/F5/F6** — planned and executed.

---

## 1 — `.mcp.json`: both servers *(one small PR, first)*

`main` tracks:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "icepanel": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.icepanel.io/mcp" } } }
```

The displaced local file configured graft as a stdio server
(`npx -y @nanonets/graft mcp`). Both belong in the tracked file — graft is
already a first-class part of how this repo is navigated (there is a
`.claude/skills/graft/` and a SessionStart hook that points at it).

**One thing that goes stale with it**, and it is the reason this is a PR and
not a one-line edit: `docs/architecture/icepanel-model.md:2030` says the file
*"names a server and nothing else"*, and
`docs/architecture/README.md:85` points at it. The sentence stops being true
the moment a second server is added, so it changes in the same commit.

Nothing validates `.mcp.json` — no script, workflow or Makefile target reads
it — so there is no check to extend.

---

## 2 — Stale issues: close what the tree proves is built

The founder's read is right, and the evidence is entirely local — which
matters, because **GitHub's secondary rate limit is currently refusing this
account's content requests**, and any plan that needs one API call per issue
will stall. The method below needs two or three reads and one write per issue
actually closed.

### The evidence, gathered without the API

Three independent signals, all computable from the tree:

| Signal | How | Found |
|---|---|---|
| A commit on `main` names the issue | `git log --format=%s` → `(#N)` | **173 distinct numbers** |
| Code or config cites the issue | `git grep '#NNN'` over `internal/ web/src/ cmd/ scripts/ deploy/` | **83 numbers** |
| The artifact the issue names exists | issue title names a file/symbol; check the tree | per issue |

Union of the first two: **197 issue numbers with implementation evidence.**
Intersecting that with the open-issue list is the candidate set.

### Why the obvious source is not usable

`specs/*/tasks.md` checkboxes look authoritative and are not.
`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/tasks.md` reports 81 done / 66 open, yet
T001–T006 are all unchecked and all plainly built — the cashback config keys,
the `blnk`/`redis` compose services, the `cashback` CI job. The checkboxes
have the same drift the issues do. **Evidence comes from code and history,
never from a checkbox.**

### How each issue is judged

- **Tier A — close.** A commit subject on `main` carries `(#N)`. That is the
  repository's own convention for "this commit did that", and an issue still
  open under one was simply never referenced by a PR body. Closed with a
  comment citing the commits.
- **Tier B — verify, then close or leave.** No commit reference, but the title
  names a concrete artifact (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go`, a route,
  a symbol). Check the artifact and its tests. `#242` is the shape of this:
  no commit cites it, and every handler it asks for exists.
- **Tier C — leave open, and list.** Anything ambiguous, anything for an
  unbuilt feature (the `003-cashback-claims` backlog, #448–#492, is not
  built), and anything where the artifact exists but the issue asks for more
  than the artifact.

Tier C is reported to the founder rather than guessed at. A wrongly closed
issue is a task that quietly stops existing.

### Rate-limit discipline

Two or three reads to list the open issues, then all judgement is local. Each
close is one `PATCH` (`state: closed`, `state_reason: completed`) plus one
comment. Batched with pauses and resumable from a written work-list, so a
secondary limit part-way through costs nothing but time.

---

## 3 — F3: the terms, and the opt-in *(two PRs)*

### 3a — `/{lang}/terms`

Its own route in the legal family — same layout, masthead and language
switcher as `/{lang}/impressum` — but **not** a fourth `LegalPane`.
`LegalPane` renders term/value pairs out of `brand.legal` (entity, address,
jurisdiction); the cashback terms are prose, and forcing them through it would
distort a component that currently does one thing well.

Content lives in a new `web/src/lib/legal/terms.ts` beside
`lib/legal/strings.ts`, in `el` and `de`, with the version rendered from
`brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
`Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`).

Each clause states a rule the code actually enforces, and nothing else:

| Clause | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| the rate shown when you clicked is the rate that applies | FR-013, the band snapshotted onto the click |
| an entry is pending until the shop confirms it | `earnings/state.go` — `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` |
| a refund reverses it, and both rows stay visible | `reversal_of_id`, US3 scenario 2 |
| money is paid only to an account proved yours | FR-051, `verified_at` |
| there is a floor before a payout | `payout_threshold` |
| leaving stops the earning and keeps the records | FR-003 — a status and a date, never a deletion |
| balances are a claim on a future rebate | founder decision Q2, ADR-0002 |

No invented obligations, no boilerplate, and the PR says plainly that
counsel-approved text replaces this before launch.

**Not** linked from the site footer. That carries the three notices a
German-facing service legally owes; these are product terms, reached from the
opt-in screen and from the wallet.

Yes, enabled — but I should give you an honest number rather than a flattering one.

**What's enabled:** the index is committed (`graft/`, 620 cards), the CLI is on PATH, there's a skill and a SessionStart hook, and the MCP tools were available this session as deferred tools. After the commit I just made, `.mcp.json` carries both graft and IcePanel, so future sessions get the MCP server too rather than depending on whose checkout you're in.

**Tokens saved this session: ~86k, from exactly one subagent.**

That's the whole tally, and the breakdown is not flattering:

| Who | graft tally |
|---|---|
| The auth/session survey | **~86,008 saved** — its own report |
| The catalogue/click-out/wallet survey | ~0 — *"the task named every file to read"* |
| The shell-exchange survey | ~0 — same reason |
| The design-canvas extraction | n/a — a 3MB HTML artifact, not source |
| **Me, directly** | **zero. I never called a graft tool.** |

I used `git grep`, `git log` and `sed` throughout. The repo's own guidance says to reach for graft first and I mostly didn't — which is a bit rich given I just wrote a commit message arguing for its place in the config.

The reason the last two agents saved nothing is instructive though, and not really a failure: I'd already located everything, so their prompts named exact files. graft's value is in *finding* code, and by then there was nothing left to find. The 86k came from the one survey where I genuinely didn't know where the auth seam lived.

Where it would have earned its keep and I skipped it: tracing `EditorSession` across 28 files for the rename (I used `git grep -l` then read each), and mapping the click-out failure paths. `graft callers` is exactly the tool for the first — the guidance even says to run it before a rename, and I didn't.

I'll use it properly for the remaining work — the click-out statuses and the wallet paging both start from "where does this actually go", which is its case.

The `.mcp.json` commit is made; let me finish that PR and move to the issue cleanup.

You were right, and I wasn't testing in the browser. I am now.

## What was actually wrong

Your browser is signed in as `editor1@example.com` — visible in the editor chrome. The chain:

1. Reader pages **deliberately resolve no session** (it costs an auth round-trip, and the front page is most of the traffic), so the chrome shows "Σύνδεση" to everyone — including you.
2. Clicking it goes to `/el/signin`, which found your session and **silently redirected you back where you came from**.
3. The page you were on is the page you ended up on. The button does nothing.

This is the part worth dwelling on. `curl https://ra1ze.com/el/signin` returns **200 with a working form** — the page is genuinely correct for a signed-out visitor. And `signin.test.ts` rendered through the container with no session, because the middleware that files one doesn't run there.

**Every one of my 27 cases tested the one visitor the page was already right for.** The redirect branch shipped completely unexercised. A hundred percent of the tests passing told me nothing about the state you were in.

## Fixed — [#584](https://github.com/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/pull/584)

The page now says who's signed in, offers a way onward, and offers sign-out (which is how you sign in as someone else). The two sign-in paths are *rendered away*, not hidden — a form in the DOM is a form that can be posted. Signing out lands back on the sign-in page and says so.

The harness can now file a session by hand (`rememberSession` is exported, the WeakMap is keyed by the request), and four new cases cover the branch. 1052 tests pass.

**Still wrong, and I've left it deliberately:** the chrome offers "sign in" to someone signed in. That's the root cause, and fixing it means either paying for a session on reader pages or a lighter-weight hint. It belongs with the member-bar work — #584 makes the product honest either way.
